s: funny, comical (chiefly dated, but still usual with certain intensifiers as in urkomisch, zu komisch, wahnsinnig komisch)
Das war sowieso ein sehr komischer Kompromiss.
It was a very weird compromise anyway.
Das war echt ein komischer Vogel.
He was a very peculiar guy.
komisch.et: Early 16th century in the sense “comedic”, directly from Latin com(icus) + -isch, from Ancient Greek κωμικός (kōmikós). The broader sense “funny” since the 17th century under influence of French comique. The sense “strange” was derived thence (as in English fu…

Komitee.et: Borrowed from French comité. First attested in the 18th century.

s: comitology (art of resolving issues by committees)
escort, retinue, especially a celebratory escort for graduating students
A county, especially the primary administrative subdivision of the historical Kingdom of Hungary or the modern parliamentary republic
